parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a universal entry-document exposure with a hostile division. The federal order and 2025 passport policy bar X markers and mismatched markers; trans travelers report confiscated/blocked passports and stranded departures, and the Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse cases casting doubt on sex and weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility — a continuous, high-probability outing mechanism with severe administrative consequences. In-division, facilities access is restricted in state buildings, no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage exists, religious-refusal service denial is lawful, marker change is barred, and minority care is banned. No imprisonment regime targets visitors here; national courts partly enjoin orders and a documented settlement shows some recourse. The totality sits in Elevated Risk: entry refusal, exclusion and hostility are realistic; imprisonment or worse is not.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order/cable: X markers barred, M/F only; officers told to refuse where doubt about sex exists and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; travelers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; eight foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding never automatic with four elements and limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate to refusal, then to a fraud inquiry that compounds across any future application or transit.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal transit-checkpoint outing (pat-downs/secondary screening); immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees; corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026; division floor debate raised solitary confinement for incarcerated trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented imprisonment of visitors for identity itself; several federal orders enjoined; prior restraint requires refusal-to-depart in the cited trespass statute.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped for document discrepancy who enters custody moves from administrative exposure into the documented harmful custody regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division's 2025 law (eff. 1 July 2025) bars trans people from matching bathrooms/locker rooms in state schools and buildings; nationwide map shows 21 units with bans, 4 with criminal triggers; national order bars federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division law carries no documented criminal penalty for visitors; 29 units plus capital district lack mapped bans; the trespass offence requires entry plus refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding order plus division law align state and national exclusion; private venues in this division remain outside the ban's text.

care_services.exposure: Division bans under-18 gender-affirming care (2023) with tapering mandate; national orders defund and stigmatise care, subpoena under-19 medical records, and cut LGBTQ youth crisis services.
care_services.protection: Care is largely resident-facing; adult emergency care denial not documented for this division; some orders blocked in court.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces division criminal-civil liability regime (private right of action to 25) plus federal funding hostility if care is sought.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal rhetoric: 'radical gender ideology' in extremism guidance, May 2026 counterterrorism priority on 'radically pro-transgender' groups, 'mutilation' framing; 66% public backing ASAB document rules; division religious-refusal service law (2021) lets businesses deny LGBTQ customers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling; rewards framework never lists gender ideology as a criterion; counterterrorism powers stated not to target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-sanctioned service refusal converts official framing into everyday traveller-facing denial with no state recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division care ban with lawsuits authorised to age 25; federal order threatening prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; sports bans; facility ban covering K-12 including off-campus activities.
minors_guardians.protection: Mostly resident/school-facing; a visiting minor not enrolled in division schools is outside much of it; national employment and hate-crime law remain.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent of a trans minor carries disclosure risk at document checks, then faces the division's care-liability regime if treatment is needed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division has no state nondiscrimination law and its hate-crime law omits gender identity; only 23 units cover GI bias crimes; documented national arrest of a trans woman (another unit, Mar 2025) held 24 hours in a men's ward.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented pattern of trans-specific killings here; national hate-crime prosecution available; division settlement with an LGBTQ organisation shows courts functioning.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state bias coverage pushes incidents into federal prosecution, which is slower and uneven.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Contested and moving rules: several orders enjoined but in force at times; division ID procedure post-March-2026 ruling unconfirmed; enforcement of facilities law in custody unresolved; 4 units flagged 'Do Not Travel'.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation (passport suit), legal-aid FAQ, running equality maps, a documented $300k settlement and non-discrimination commitment, functioning federal courts granting relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate federal overreach but do not repeal the division's own exclusions or service-refusal laws.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register excludes trans visitors administratively with no remedy. This dossier's passport regime plus the Feb 2025 refusal cable produces comparable entry exclusion and stranding, but with pending litigation, waivers and no single uniform register — slightly higher than 0.35-A overall.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening ending in refusal with slow appeals — friction, not punishment. Here screening is backed by a categorical marker ban, documented passport confiscation and a possible lifetime fraud finding, making entry exposure materially worse than 0.55-B.

Vesskar's routine verification with inconsistent enforcement, thin legal aid and detention for mismatched presentation closely matches this combined regime: universal document exposure, administrative holds, unpredictable outcomes, no credible imprisonment pathway for ordinary visitors.

Vellmaris shows mismatched-document stops cured by national equality law and working complaints. This jurisdiction lacks state equality law, its hate-crime law omits gender identity, and its federal posture is hostile — clearly below 0.65-A despite functioning courts.

parsed.synthesis: Outing probability is high and structurally engineered: the entry-document regime reaches every trans visitor at passport control, and the 2025 cable converts discrepancy into refusal and possible lifetime ineligibility. Severity after discovery, however, is administrative-plus-social rather than custodial: exclusion, stranding, facility denial in state buildings, lawful service refusal, and a hostile climate (66% backing ASAB documents), but no documented imprisonment of visitors for identity, functioning federal courts that have enjoined several orders and delivered at least one settlement. The division adds exclusions (facilities, marker change, care, no state protections) without its own criminal penalty for visitors. Custody harm is real but contingent on entering detention — an escalation path from document discrepancy that lowers the score below the friction band but stops short of the severe-custody anchors.
